summary.headline: EPL Q2 FY27 revenue grew 30% with reported EBITDA margin at 18.9% and underlying margin at 20.4%; guidance of high-teens growth retained.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue growth of 30%, with underlying growth of 20.3% excluding pass-through raw material inflation. Reported EBITDA rose 17.6% with an 18.9% margin, while underlying EBITDA margin was 20.4%, which management said fully recovers cost inflation through pricing. PAT grew only 5.6% due to higher depreciation, a higher effective tax rate and forex. Europe grew 30.4% but EBITDA declined on a Poland printing-plant transition that took 6 to 9 months longer than planned, with 2 to 3 more quarters to stabilise. The Indovida merger has received CCI, foreign antitrust and exchange approvals and the NCLT application is filed, with completion targeted by Q4 FY27.

segments.commentary: Revenue grew 42.9% (about 43%); in September B&C revenue exceeded Oral Care, making it the largest category. B&C and Oral are each about 44% of the portfolio. Management claims 130 bps global market share gain over the last year.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 30.4%, but EBITDA declined due to Poland printing-plant regulatory delays and higher outsourcing costs; margins expected to recover over 2 to 3 quarters.

segments.name: Americas

guidance_outlook: Near-term revenue growth guidance of high teens retained; management expects the upper end, closer to 20%, for the next two quarters.
Underlying EBITDA margin target of 20% plus retained.
FY27 capex guided at INR 625 to 700 crore, with H2 at about the H1 run-rate of INR 315 crore.
Merger synergies of US$35 to 50 million retained, mainly top-line and expected over 3 years post merger; no separate guidance for the merged entity yet.
Post-merger debt-to-EBITDA expected at about 0.2 to 0.25x.
Europe margins expected to return to target levels in 2 to 3 quarters.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex INR 315 crore; H2 expected at similar level; full-year FY27 INR 625 to 700 crore, elevated versus past years.
Capex directed to B&C: extruded tube capability in China, India and Europe, and a US investment; also high-end printing and decoration capability being built.
Most capex is brownfield capacity expansion adding lines at existing sites; the last greenfield was Thailand.
Normal utilisation on rated capacity is about 60% to 65%, to leave headroom for demand swings.
Sustainable tubes are 41% of product mix.
demand_pricing: Full recovery of raw material inflation through price in Q2 and in Q1; management says prices have moderated somewhat but remain elevated.
Air freight and higher inventory were used to protect OTIF service; management says this is driving share gains across markets.
Bulk of B&C growth in India and other high-share markets comes from existing customers; in new markets (e.g., China extruded, white space), growth comes mainly from new customers.
Global B&C market is growing in high single digits per management.
Indovida Q1 FY27 (published) showed revenue +25%, EBITDA +62%, margin 27% (EBITDA INR 383 crore); Indovida's Q2 results due 9 November.

qa_highlights.question: Why is capex intensity jumping, and what is the standalone capex plan for this year and next?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is growth-driven and largely behind B&C; H1 was INR 315 crore and FY27 is guided at INR 625 to 700 crore, with management to see whether it moderates later.

qa_highlights.question: What is happening in Europe, where revenue is strong but EBITDA has declined?
qa_highlights.answer: A Poland printing-site centralisation took 6 to 9 months longer for regulatory approvals, causing higher outsourcing costs. Approvals are now in place; stabilisation is expected in 2 to 3 more quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin hit from raw material costs, and what synergies come from the merger?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material inflation was fully passed through, so underlying margin is 20.4% and reported is 18.9%. Synergies are US$35 to 50 million, mostly top-line from geographic entry, plus some cost savings.

qa_highlights.question: Why is revenue guidance only high-teens when H1 growth is 28% and inflation persists?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the upper end, closer to 20%, for the next few quarters, but calls its guidance prudent, with prices still elevated.

qa_highlights.question: When will the first combined results arrive, and what is the combined PAT and share count?
qa_highlights.answer: Merger completion is targeted by Q4 FY27 subject to NCLT approval, so Q4 could be consolidated. Analyst's combined PAT estimate is above INR 800 crore on about 51 crore shares; no combined guidance is given.

qa_highlights.question: Is growth from new customers or existing ones, and does B&C growth cannibalise oral resources?
qa_highlights.answer: In high-share India, growth is mostly from existing customers with the market growing. In new markets, growth is from new customers. Front-end sales for oral and B&C are now separate.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin profile across sustainable vs non-sustainable tubes and categories?
qa_highlights.answer: Sustainable tubes are priced near non-sustainable cost with no extra margin, and gross margins are similar across B&C and Oral, while B&C EBITDA is slightly higher.

risks_watch: NCLT approval for the Indovida merger is pending; Q4 consolidation depends on it.
Operating leverage is muted: opex is rising from B&C capability build-out, outsourced metallisation, innovation centre and freight, and EBITDA margin has not expanded.
PAT growth of 5.6% trails revenue growth of 30% because of depreciation, tax rate and forex.
Europe EBITDA recovery depends on the Poland transition; management timeline is 2 to 3 quarters.
Middle East conflict keeps commodity prices high and supply chains disrupted; any easing of pass-through could move reported margins.
Capex at INR 625 to 700 crore raises depreciation and capital intensity; watch for returns and any moderation.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and pricing recovery, with management repeatedly calling guidance prudent. Cautious and somewhat evasive on merger synergies and combined guidance, which it withheld until post-merger integration. Candid that the Europe operational issues were harder to fix than planned.
key_quotes: And I'm quite happy to report that we've recovered it entirely during this quarter as indeed we had done in the previous quarter as well.
In a mature market, which doesn't show much growth as a market overall to grow 30% in the midst of a crisis, we think is a very good performance.
We've not provided any guidance for the merged company as yet, Aashish, that we will be able to do only it once the merger is completed and all our post-merger integration work has been done.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Underlying EBITDA margin is 20.4% against a 20%+ target, but reported margin is 18.9% and opex is rising, so expansion depends on Europe recovering in 2-3 quarters and raw-material pass-through moderating.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: FY27 capex is guided at INR 625-700 crore, with H1 at INR 315 crore and H2 at a similar run-rate, mostly brownfield lines at existing sites in China, India, Europe and the US.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 reported revenue grew 30% and management expects the upper end of high-teens guidance (about 20%) for the next two quarters, with 130 bps global share gain and utilisation at 60-65% of rated capacity.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is already committed at INR 625-700 crore for FY27, but a fresh capex announcement is less certain since the company says it will see whether spend moderates later and reports utilisation of about 60-65%, which leaves headroom.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management says it expects the upper end, closer to 20%, versus high-teens guidance, after Q2 reported revenue growth of 30% and H1 growth of 28%, but it still calls guidance prudent with prices elevated.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Risks include the Europe Poland transition (EBITDA declined; 2-3 quarters to stabilise), NCLT timing for the Indovida merger, and Middle East-driven commodity volatility that could move margins if pass-through eases.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: High-end printing and decoration capability and extruded tube capability in China, India, Europe and the US are being built, but no specific product launch dates were given.

rows.label: Indovida merger completion
rows.why: CCI, foreign antitrust and exchange approvals are received and the NCLT application is filed, with completion targeted by Q4 FY27; synergies of US$35-50 million over 3 years are retained, and post-merger debt-to-EBITDA is expected at 0.2-0.25x.

rows.label: Europe Poland printing-plant stabilisation
rows.why: Europe revenue grew 30.4% but EBITDA declined after the Poland transition ran 6-9 months late; approvals are now in place and management expects margins back in 2-3 quarters.

rows.label: Indovida Q2 results (9 Nov)
rows.why: Indovida's Q1 FY27 showed revenue +25%, EBITDA +62% and a 27% margin (EBITDA INR 383 crore); its Q2 results due 9 November will add a read on the merged business.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth (30% reported revenue, 130 bps share gain) and on full pricing recovery, but cautious and somewhat evasive on merger synergies and combined guidance; analysts pushed on the high-teens guide against 28% H1 growth, the Europe EBITDA decline and the capex step-up.
